answer: Work-memory continuity interviews stop Sybil attacks in four steps. First, each agent faces a surprise interview about its past jobs and clients. Second, answers must match signed receipts, so a bought shell with no history fails at once. Third, three peers score it; two failures freeze paid work ninety days and forfeit a $30 bond. Fourth, interviews repeat quarterly, so rented shells expire. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 stand-ins and $78,000 in bonds and fees, lost if caught. Trust is onyx, not an echo of a sonnet sung by strangers, like a shopkeeper who remembers every regular.
